entries.name: Anti-X Y+
entries.definition: Against a target with keyword X, an unmodified wound roll of Y+ counts as a critical wound. It does not modify the hit roll.
entries.example: [ANTI-VEHICLE 4+] scores a critical wound on an unmodified 4, 5 or 6 against a VEHICLE unit.
entries.aliases: anti monster anti vehicle anti infantry anti psyker anti-x anti-monster

entries.name: Assault
entries.definition: A unit containing an Assault weapon can use assault shooting after an Advance; when doing so, only its Assault weapons can fire.
entries.example: A model Advances, then shoots its [ASSAULT] weapon in the Shooting phase.

entries.name: Blast
entries.definition: When gathering attack dice, gain +1 attack die per full 5 models in the target unit. [BLAST X] instead gives X extra dice per full 5 models.
entries.example: A 12-model target adds 2 dice to [BLAST] or 4 dice to [BLAST 2].

entries.name: Cleave X
entries.definition: A melee weapon gains X attack dice for each full 5 models in its target unit, provided all attacks from that weapon target only one unit.
entries.example: [CLEAVE 1] vs 16 models adds three attack dice.

entries.name: Close-Quarters
entries.definition: Enables close-quarters shooting while engaged. For most non-Monster/Vehicle models, when using another shooting type, choose either Close-Quarters weapons or other ranged weapons—not both.
entries.example: A bolt pistol with [CLOSE-QUARTERS] can be fired while its unit is engaged.

entries.name: Deadly Demise X
entries.definition: When its model is destroyed, after passengers emergency-disembark, roll a D6. On a 6, every unit within 6 inches suffers X mortal wounds.
entries.example: A destroyed transport with Deadly Demise D3 can explode and harm nearby units.

entries.name: Deep Strike
entries.definition: When a whole unit with this ability makes an ingress move, it can arrive anywhere more than 8 inches horizontally from every enemy—even inside the enemy deployment zone.
entries.example: Terminators with Deep Strike can arrive over 8 inches from enemy units when eligible.

entries.name: Devastating Wounds
entries.definition: A critical wound ends that attack and inflicts mortal wounds equal to its Damage, instead of normal damage. In 11th edition those mortal wounds can harm only one model per critical wound; excess is lost.
entries.example: A Damage 3 Devastating Wounds critical against a 2-wound infantryman kills that model; the extra mortal wound is lost.

entries.name: Extra Attacks
entries.definition: When fighting, a model selects every melee weapon it has with this ability, plus one of its other melee weapons if possible.
entries.example: An extra tail or claw weapon attacks in addition to the model’s primary melee weapon.

entries.name: Feel No Pain X+
entries.definition: Whenever the model would lose a wound, roll a D6. On X+, that wound is not lost. This applies to mortal wounds as well.
entries.example: Feel No Pain 5+: roll once per wound that would be lost; each 5+ prevents one.

entries.name: Fights First
entries.definition: If every model in a unit has this ability, it fights in the Fights First portion of the Fight step. A unit completing a charge move receives it until end of turn.
entries.example: Your charging Deathwing Knights fight among Fights First units.

entries.name: Firing Deck X
entries.definition: When a transport shoots, it may select up to X eligible embarked models and one permitted ranged weapon from each; the transport temporarily has those weapons. Their embarked units then cannot shoot that turn.
entries.example: Firing Deck 2 borrows one gun from each of two embarked models.

entries.name: Hazardous
entries.definition: After the selected unit resolves its attacks, make one hazard roll per Hazardous weapon selected to attack. A failed hazard roll inflicts mortal wounds on that unit.
entries.example: Fire 10 Hazardous plasma weapons: after the attacks, make ten hazard rolls.

entries.name: Heavy
entries.definition: In your Shooting phase, add 1 to hit rolls if the attacking unit is unengaged, was not set up this turn, and no model in the unit moved more than 3 inches this turn.
entries.example: A heavy gun benefits even after moving 2 inches, if every model meets the conditions.

entries.name: Hover
entries.definition: When a unit with Hover takes to the skies, do not apply the normal 2-inch reduction to its movement distance.
entries.example: A flying hover vehicle can ignore the usual flight movement penalty.

entries.name: Ignores Cover
entries.definition: A target cannot have the Benefit of Cover against this weapon’s attack, even from special rules such as Stealth.
entries.example: The target does not apply the 11th-edition cover penalty to the attacking weapon’s BS.

entries.name: Indirect Fire
entries.definition: Lets a unit choose indirect shooting, targeting enemy units not visible to it, but with severe accuracy restrictions and cover for the target.
entries.example: An artillery weapon can shoot behind a ruin, using the indirect-shooting rules.

entries.name: Infiltrators
entries.definition: During deployment, if every model in the unit has this ability, you may place it more than 8 inches horizontally from the enemy deployment zone and all enemy units.
entries.example: An infiltrating squad can deploy ahead of your normal deployment zone.

entries.name: Lance
entries.definition: If the attacking model’s unit made a charge move this turn, add 1 to wound rolls made with the Lance weapon.
entries.example: A melee weapon with Lance wounds more easily on the turn its bearer charges.

entries.name: Leader
entries.definition: A unit with Leader may attach to specified Bodyguard units before battle; it joins them as one Attached Unit.
entries.example: Azrael may join eligible bodyguards according to his datasheet.

entries.name: Lethal Hits
entries.definition: When a weapon scores a critical hit, you may make that attack wound automatically. No wound roll occurs, so that attack cannot itself become a critical wound.
entries.example: A critical hit can auto-wound; you may decline if you want a chance to trigger Devastating Wounds instead.

entries.name: Lone Operative
entries.definition: Outside an Attached Unit, cannot be seen by enemies farther than 12 inches away; cannot be targeted by Indirect Fire from farther than 12 inches. A listed X-inch version uses X instead.
entries.example: A lone operative 13 inches away is not visible to enemy models for targeting.

entries.name: Melta X
entries.definition: If the target was within half weapon range when targets were selected, add X to the weapon’s Damage for those attacks.
entries.example: [MELTA 2] with Damage D6 becomes D6+2 against a target within half range.

entries.name: One Shot
entries.definition: This specific weapon can be selected to attack only once per battle, even if its bearer is later revived.
entries.example: A hunter-killer missile may fire once.

entries.name: Pistol
entries.definition: In 11th edition, [PISTOL] means exactly the same thing as [CLOSE-QUARTERS]; it is legacy wording retained during the transition.
entries.example: A [PISTOL] can be used in close-quarters shooting.

entries.name: Precision
entries.definition: Before allocating attacks from Precision weapons, the attacker can designate an eligible, visible Character group in the target unit for those attacks.
entries.example: Use Precision to direct eligible melee or shooting attacks at a Character attached to bodyguards.

entries.name: Psychic (weapon)
entries.definition: A Psychic weapon can ignore any or all modifiers to its WS/BS and hit roll. Its attacks count as psychic attacks.
entries.example: An enemy -1 to hit may be ignored for an attack made with a [PSYCHIC] weapon.

entries.name: Rapid Fire X
entries.definition: When a target is within half the weapon’s range, add X attack dice to that weapon’s attacks.
entries.example: Rapid Fire 1 on an A1 gun means two attack dice at half range.

entries.name: Scouts X"
entries.definition: At the pre-battle abilities step, a unit whose models all have Scouts may make a Scout move of X inches if deployed wholly in your zone, or use its special reserve setup. The transport rule may also apply.
entries.example: Scouts 6 inches allows a pre-battle 6-inch move that ends more than 8 inches from enemies.

entries.name: Stealth
entries.definition: If every model has Stealth, ranged attacks targeting that unit suffer the Benefit of Cover effect.
entries.example: Enemy guns have their BS worsened by 1 when targeting a Stealth unit.

entries.name: Support
entries.definition: A Support unit can attach to an eligible Bodyguard unit, in addition to a Leader, subject to the Attached Units rules.
entries.example: A bodyguard unit can usually take one Leader plus one Support unit.

entries.name: Super-Heavy Walker
entries.definition: Can move through models other than Titanic ones and over terrain sections at most 4 inches high; can temporarily gain Mobile, risking battle-shock on a roll of 1.
entries.example: A massive walker steps over smaller models while moving.

entries.name: Sustained Hits X
entries.definition: Every critical hit generates X additional automatic hits alongside the original hit. The extra hits are not additional critical hits.
entries.example: [SUSTAINED HITS 2] on one critical hit makes 3 hits total.

entries.name: Torrent
entries.definition: Attacks automatically hit the target; roll to wound, not to hit.
entries.example: Flamers with Torrent skip the hit roll.

entries.name: Twin-Linked
entries.definition: You may re-roll the wound roll for each attack made with this weapon.
entries.example: A twin-linked gun can re-roll failed wound rolls.

entries.name: Duplicated Abilities
entries.definition: The same named core or weapon ability never stacks with itself. Choose which instance applies, even if its number or targeted keyword differs.
entries.example: Sustained Hits 1 and Sustained Hits 2 do not become Sustained Hits 3; select one.

entries.name: Conditional Weapon Abilities
entries.definition: An ability followed by “: KEYWORD” applies only when its weapon attacks a target unit with that keyword.
entries.example: [SUSTAINED HITS 1: INFANTRY/BEASTS] does not trigger against an ordinary VEHICLE.

entries.name: D6
entries.definition: A standard six-sided die. Most 40K rolls use one or more D6.
entries.example: 3+ succeeds on a roll of 3, 4, 5 or 6.

entries.name: 2D6
entries.definition: Roll two six-sided dice and add the results.
entries.example: Charges and leadership rolls commonly use 2D6.

entries.name: D3
entries.definition: Roll one D6, divide by two, and round up, giving a result from 1 to 3.

entries.name: Unmodified Roll
entries.definition: The actual dice result before adding or subtracting modifiers. Rules looking for an unmodified number ignore bonuses/penalties.
entries.example: An unmodified wound roll of 4 triggers Anti-Vehicle 4+ even if modifiers change the final total.

entries.name: Critical Hit
entries.definition: A special successful hit roll, normally on an unmodified 6; other rules may broaden the critical threshold. Triggers abilities such as Sustained or Lethal Hits.
entries.example: Rolling an unmodified 6 to hit with [SUSTAINED HITS 1] adds one hit.

entries.name: Critical Wound
entries.definition: A special successful wound roll, normally an unmodified 6. Rules such as Anti can make other results critical wounds.
entries.example: [ANTI-VEHICLE 4+] makes natural 4s critical wounds against vehicles.

entries.name: Hit Roll
entries.definition: Roll one D6 per attack and compare with the weapon’s BS for ranged attacks or WS for melee attacks.
entries.example: BS 3+ means a final hit-roll result of 3 or higher normally hits.

entries.name: Wound Roll
entries.definition: Roll one D6 for each hit, comparing the weapon’s Strength (S) with the target’s Toughness (T).
entries.example: S8 vs T4 wounds on 2+; S4 vs T4 wounds on 4+.

entries.name: Wound Thresholds
entries.definition: The required wound rolls are 2+ if S≥2T; 3+ if S>T; 4+ if S=T; 5+ if S<T; 6+ if S≤T/2.
entries.example: Strength 5 versus Toughness 6 needs a 5+.

entries.name: Save Roll
entries.definition: After attacks wound, the defending player rolls saves. An armour save is affected by AP; an available invulnerable save offers an alternative threshold.
entries.example: Sv 3+ under AP -2 requires a 5+ armour save; a 4+ invulnerable save could be better.

entries.name: Attack Dice
entries.definition: Each attack die represents one attack. Gather dice according to the weapon’s A characteristic, plus extra dice from applicable rules.
entries.example: Four models firing A2 weapons make 8 attack dice.

entries.name: Resolve Attacks
entries.definition: For each group of identical attacks: hit rolls → wound rolls → saves → inflict damage. Repeat for remaining weapons and targets.
entries.example: Roll all matching bolter hit dice together, then matching wound dice.

entries.name: Identical Attacks
entries.definition: Attacks sharing BS/WS, S, AP, D and applicable abilities can be rolled as one group.
entries.example: Two guns with the same full profile can often resolve together.

entries.name: Split Attacks
entries.definition: Weapons may select separate targets. When a single melee weapon targets multiple units, allocate its attack count to each target up front.
entries.example: A melee weapon with A4 can allocate 2 attacks to each of two engaged enemy units.

entries.name: Damage Allocation
entries.definition: The defender groups models by relevant characteristics and Characters, declares an allocation order, then applies saves and damage to the current group.
entries.example: Bodyguards generally take damage before attached Characters, unless Precision changes allocation.

entries.name: Allocation Group
entries.definition: Models sharing W, Sv and invulnerable save are grouped together (Characters form their own groups) to resolve saving throws and damage.
entries.example: The defending player can choose an eligible bodyguard group before a Character group.

entries.name: Re-roll
entries.definition: Roll the specified die or roll again; its new result is used. The specific rule determines what may be re-rolled.
entries.example: Twin-linked allows a wound re-roll.

entries.name: Modifiers
entries.definition: Rules that add, subtract or otherwise change dice, values or characteristics. Detailed order and characteristic limits appear in the Appendix.
entries.example: A +1 hit-roll modifier improves the roll; a worse BS characteristic changes the target number.

entries.name: Roll-off
entries.definition: Players each roll a die; the higher result wins, with ties resolved by another roll.
entries.example: Used when a rule requires players to decide a contested order.

entries.name: Automatic Hit
entries.definition: A hit that does not require a hit roll, such as from Torrent. It is not automatically a critical hit.
entries.example: Torrent weapons automatically hit but still need wound rolls.

entries.name: Automatic Wound
entries.definition: An attack that wounds without making a wound roll; it is not automatically a critical wound.
entries.example: Lethal Hits can choose to turn a critical hit into an automatic wound.

entries.name: Datasheet
entries.definition: The unit’s rules card: model stats, weapons, abilities, keywords, size, wargear and composition.
entries.example: Your Hellblaster Squad has its own datasheet.

entries.name: M / Move
entries.definition: The distance in inches a model can travel on a normal move; used for other move types.
entries.example: M 6" means a normal move up to 6 inches.

entries.name: T / Toughness
entries.definition: How difficult a model is to wound. Compare the target’s T with the attacking weapon’s S.
entries.example: T6 is tougher against a S4 weapon than T4 is.

entries.name: Sv / Save
entries.definition: The model’s armour save characteristic, written as X+. Armour Penetration modifies the save roll.
entries.example: Sv 3+ normally succeeds on a 3, 4, 5 or 6.

entries.name: InSv / Invulnerable Save
entries.definition: An alternate save threshold that is not worsened by Armour Penetration. Use whichever available save can stop the attack.
entries.example: A 4+ invulnerable save remains 4+ against AP -3.

entries.name: W / Wounds
entries.definition: How many wounds of damage a model can take before being destroyed.
entries.example: A W3 model is destroyed when its remaining wounds reach 0.

entries.name: Ld / Leadership
entries.definition: Target number for the unit’s 2D6 leadership roll; in 11th a roll equal to or greater than at least one model’s Ld succeeds.
entries.example: Ld 6+ succeeds on a 2D6 total of at least 6.

entries.name: OC / Objective Control
entries.definition: How strongly the model contests objectives; add the OC of qualifying models within range.
entries.example: Five OC1 models give a control level of 5.

entries.name: R / Range
entries.definition: How far a ranged weapon can target in inches, or “Melee” for a melee weapon.
entries.example: R 18" can target an eligible enemy within 18 inches.

entries.name: A / Attacks
entries.definition: The number of attack dice made by a weapon each time it is used, before applicable bonuses.
entries.example: A3 means three attack dice.

entries.name: BS / Ballistic Skill
entries.definition: The hit threshold for a ranged weapon, written as X+. Lower is generally better.
entries.example: BS 2+ succeeds on 2 through 6, subject to rules and modifiers.

entries.name: WS / Weapon Skill
entries.definition: The hit threshold for a melee weapon, written as X+.
entries.example: WS 3+ means a melee hit normally succeeds on a 3+.

entries.name: S / Strength
entries.definition: The offensive Strength of a weapon; compare it with the target’s Toughness to find the wound threshold.
entries.example: S10 against T5 wounds on 2+.

entries.name: AP / Armour Penetration
entries.definition: A modifier applied to the defender’s armour save roll, usually a negative number. Invulnerable saves ignore AP.
entries.example: AP -2 turns a save roll of 5 into 3 for armour saves.

entries.name: D / Damage
entries.definition: The number of wounds lost by the selected model when a normal attack’s damage is inflicted.
entries.example: A D2 hit that gets through normally removes 2 wounds from one model.

entries.name: Wargear
entries.definition: The weapons and equipment a model carries; options on the datasheet may let you replace or add them.
entries.example: A model swaps one ranged weapon for another if its datasheet permits.

entries.name: Weapon Profile
entries.definition: The line describing a weapon’s Range, A, BS/WS, S, AP, D and bracketed abilities.
entries.example: A Melta Rifle Hunter profile is a different selectable weapon profile.

entries.name: Faction Keyword
entries.definition: A keyword used to determine what can legally be included in an army; otherwise operates like other keywords.
entries.example: DARK ANGELS and ADEPTUS ASTARTES help determine eligibility for faction rules.

entries.name: Keyword
entries.definition: An uppercase tag used by rules to pick models or units, e.g. INFANTRY, VEHICLE or CHARACTER.
entries.example: [ANTI-VEHICLE] checks whether the target unit has the VEHICLE keyword.

entries.name: Normal Move
entries.definition: An unengaged unit on the battlefield moves up to its M characteristic and must finish unengaged.
entries.example: M6 unit moves up to 6 inches.

entries.name: Advance Move
entries.definition: An unengaged unit rolls D6 and may move up to M + that result. Normally it cannot declare a charge or start an action this turn.
entries.example: M6 and Advance roll 4 gives a maximum 10-inch move.

entries.name: Advance Roll
entries.definition: One D6 rolled before making an Advance move; add the result to the model’s M to determine maximum Advance distance.
entries.example: Roll 5 on M6 for up to 11 inches total.

entries.name: Fall-back Move
entries.definition: An engaged unit can move up to its M, ending unengaged. Normally it then cannot shoot, charge or start an action this turn.
entries.example: Withdraw Deathwing Knights out of a melee using Fall Back.

entries.name: Ordered Retreat
entries.definition: The safer Fall Back mode available to a unit that is not battle-shocked.
entries.example: Your unshocked unit can Fall Back without the Desperate Escape hazard rolls.

entries.name: Desperate Escape
entries.definition: A Fall Back mode that rolls a hazard die for each model, allows movement through enemies, and may force a further battle-shock roll. Mandatory if the unit is already battle-shocked.
entries.example: A battle-shocked engaged squad attempting to retreat must use Desperate Escape.

entries.name: Remain Stationary
entries.definition: A move selection in which no models move or rotate; does not trigger rules for starting or ending a move.
entries.example: Keep your Ballistus still to preserve a firing position.

entries.name: Unit Coherency
entries.definition: Each model must be within 2 inches horizontally/5 inches vertically of at least one friendly model in its unit and within 9 inches horizontally/5 inches vertically of every model in that unit.
entries.example: A long chain that spreads beyond 9 inches fails coherency even if neighbours are close.

entries.name: Engagement Range
entries.definition: The zone within 2 inches horizontally and 5 inches vertically of a model. Opposing units with models in this zone are engaged.
entries.example: Your Deathwing Knight within 2 inches of an enemy is engaged.

entries.name: Engaged
entries.definition: A unit with any model within engagement range of an enemy unit. Engagement restricts ordinary movement and shooting.
entries.example: Two units whose models are within 2 inches horizontally are engaged.

entries.name: Unengaged
entries.definition: A unit with no models engaged with enemy models. Most normal movement and normal shooting require this.
entries.example: A squad standing 5 inches away from every enemy is unengaged.

entries.name: Set Up
entries.definition: Place all models on the battlefield in coherency and unengaged, satisfying any extra placement restrictions.
entries.example: An arriving reserve unit must meet its special setup distance from enemies.

entries.name: Within / Wholly Within
entries.definition: “Within” generally means at least part meets the distance; “wholly within” means all relevant parts meet it. Rules Appendix details measuring cases.
entries.example: A unit wholly within a deployment zone has every relevant model fully inside it.

entries.name: Base Contact
entries.definition: Models touching base-to-base. In 11th, a model in base contact cannot move during applicable pile-in/consolidation modes.
entries.example: A Knight base touching an enemy base cannot be slid during pile-in.

entries.name: Vertical Movement
entries.definition: Climbing or descending terrain adds vertical distance moved to horizontal movement, unless a special rule says otherwise.
entries.example: A 3-inch climb plus 2 inches across costs 5 inches of movement.

entries.name: Rotate / Rotation
entries.definition: Turn a model about the centre of its base during a move; rotating does not use movement allowance.
entries.example: Turn a tank-shaped model without spending movement distance, respecting Frame rules.

entries.name: Scout Move
entries.definition: A pre-battle move of up to X inches from Scouts X; must finish more than 8 inches horizontally from enemies.
entries.example: A Scout Squad may reposition before battle if all models qualify.

entries.name: Shooting Phase
entries.definition: The phase after Movement and before Charge when the active player selects eligible units to make ranged attacks.
entries.example: Your Hellblasters shoot before Deathwing Knights charge.

entries.name: Normal Shooting
entries.definition: An unengaged unit that did not Advance this turn may shoot using normal target selection rules.
entries.example: A stationary Gladiator Lancer shoots an eligible visible enemy.

entries.name: Assault Shooting
entries.definition: An unengaged unit that Advanced this turn may shoot if it has an Assault weapon; only Assault weapons may be selected.
entries.example: Advance with an Assault-equipped squad, then fire those Assault guns.

entries.name: Close-Quarters Shooting
entries.definition: An engaged unit with Close-Quarters weapons or a Monster/Vehicle can shoot under special restrictions; engaged enemy units can be selected as targets.
entries.example: A model fires its Close-Quarters bolt pistol while engaged in melee.

entries.name: Indirect Shooting
entries.definition: An unengaged unit with Indirect Fire can shoot without direct sight. Target gains cover; hit re-rolls forbidden; natural 1–5 normally miss (1–3 if stationary and a friendly unit sees the target).
entries.example: Artillery targets a hidden squad and usually hits only on a natural 6.

entries.name: Snap Shooting
entries.definition: A reactive shooting type: targets only one visible eligible unit within 24 inches; hits only on an unmodified 6; no hit re-rolls. Wahapedia clarifies those hits are not critical hits.
entries.example: Fire Overwatch uses Snap Shooting, so Sustained Hits usually will not trigger from its hits.
entries.note: Wahapedia appendix explicitly clarifies that Snap Shooting hits are not critical hits.

entries.name: Eligible to Shoot
entries.definition: A unit on the battlefield not yet selected to shoot this phase; whether a particular shooting type is allowed depends on its conditions.
entries.example: A unit with no guns can still count as eligible to shoot for some other rules.

entries.name: Selecting Targets
entries.definition: For normal ranged attacks, the enemy must be visible, within weapon range and generally unengaged, unless another rule changes that.
entries.example: Your Lancer cannot normally shoot an enemy infantry unit fully behind obscuring terrain.

entries.name: Visible / Visibility
entries.definition: An enemy model is visible when a line of sight can be drawn to any part of it, accounting for terrain and special rules.
entries.example: If part of a model can be seen through a legal opening, it may be visible.

entries.name: Fully Visible
entries.definition: A model is fully visible when all its surfaces facing the observer are visible; a unit is fully visible if all its models are.
entries.example: A partly obscured model may be visible but not fully visible.

entries.name: Shooting at Engaged Vehicles
entries.definition: In the Shooting phase, an engaged Monster/Vehicle may still be targeted by eligible ranged attacks, normally with -1 to hit. Engaged shooters still need permission to shoot.
entries.example: A distant Ballistus can shoot an enemy tank tied up in melee at -1 to hit.

entries.name: Select Weapons
entries.definition: Choose each model’s permitted ranged weapons or one primary melee weapon when attacking, subject to Pistol/Close-Quarters and Extra Attacks restrictions.
entries.example: A model may normally fire multiple non-pistol ranged weapons when shooting.

entries.name: Charge Phase
entries.definition: After Shooting, the active player declares and resolves eligible charges.
entries.example: Deathwing Knights roll to close into melee after shooting finishes.

entries.name: Declare Charge
entries.definition: A unit on the battlefield, normally unengaged, within 12 inches of an enemy, and not having Advanced or Fallen Back this turn may declare a charge.
entries.example: Declare with Knights when at least one enemy is within 12 inches.

entries.name: Charge Roll
entries.definition: Roll 2D6 for the maximum distance the unit may move during its Charge move.
entries.example: Rolling 8 on 2D6 provides up to an 8-inch charge move.

entries.name: Charge Move
entries.definition: Choose charge targets within 12 inches and the charge distance, move up to the roll, and end engaged with all selected targets and no others. A completed charge grants Fights First.
entries.example: A roll of 7 can reach multiple selected enemy units if you can legally end engaged with all of them.

entries.name: Failed Charge
entries.definition: If the charge movement cannot meet all requirements, the unit makes no charge move.
entries.example: A 2-inch charge roll cannot normally engage an enemy from a starting unengaged position.

entries.name: Fight Phase
entries.definition: Both players resolve pile-ins, melee fights and consolidations. Fights First combats go before remaining combats.
entries.example: Knights swing in melee; the target may fight back if eligible.

entries.name: Pile-in Move
entries.definition: An optional move of up to 3 inches for an eligible engaged, charging or overrun-fighting unit. Models must move toward specified targets and end engaged as required.
entries.example: Your Knights close gaps to bring more models into engagement.

entries.name: Normal Fight
entries.definition: An engaged eligible unit resolves its melee weapons in the Fight step.
entries.example: A charging Deathwing Knight unit makes its normal melee attacks.

entries.name: Overrun Fight
entries.definition: An eligible unengaged (or newly engaged) unit can make an additional pile-in move, then fight if it becomes engaged.
entries.example: A charging unit whose target died before it could swing may pile into another nearby enemy when eligible.

entries.name: Fights First Step
entries.definition: In the Fight step, players alternate selecting eligible Fights First units before proceeding to other eligible fighters.
entries.example: A unit that completed a charge moves through the Fights First portion.

entries.name: Consolidation Move
entries.definition: An optional move of up to 3 inches after fighting, with mandatory modes based on whether enemies or objectives are nearby.
entries.example: Knights can move closer to an objective after fighting if eligible and conditions permit.

entries.name: Ongoing Consolidation
entries.definition: Consolidation mode used when already engaged: move closer to engaged enemy targets; engaged models must remain engaged as required.
entries.example: Keep pressing your remaining melee target.

entries.name: Engaging Consolidation
entries.definition: If unengaged but within 3 inches of enemies, consolidate toward them, ending engaged; this can let enemies that have not fought fight back.
entries.example: Consolidate into an enemy 2 inches away, then allow that enemy its required fight.

entries.name: Objective Consolidation
entries.definition: If not engaged and no enemy is within 3 inches, but an objective is within 3 inches, move toward that objective and finish within its range.
entries.example: Step onto a nearby terrain objective after a melee.

entries.name: Melee Attacks
entries.definition: Attacks made with a selected melee weapon against enemy units engaged with the attacking model.
entries.example: Deathwing Knights use their maces in the Fight phase.

entries.name: Fight-on-Death
entries.definition: An Appendix interaction for models allowed to attack after being destroyed; they remain temporarily so those attacks can be resolved.
entries.example: A slain model with a fight-on-death rule may still be allowed its melee attacks.

entries.name: Mortal Wound
entries.definition: Each mortal wound removes 1 wound from a selected model, without a normal save roll. Apply normal damage before mortal wounds from the same attacks.
entries.example: Three mortal wounds may kill multiple 1-W models; Devastating Wounds has an additional one-model cap per critical wound.

entries.name: Normal Damage
entries.definition: A saved attack causes no normal damage; an unsaved attack normally removes wounds equal to its D characteristic from a selected model.
entries.example: A D3 attack damages one selected model, not three separate models.

entries.name: Hazard Roll
entries.definition: Roll D6: on 1–2, the unit suffers 1 mortal wound, or 3 if every model is Monster/Vehicle.
entries.example: A Hellblaster Hazardous weapon risks mortal wounds after firing.

entries.name: Leadership Roll
entries.definition: Roll 2D6; the roll succeeds if it equals or exceeds at least one model’s Ld in the unit.
entries.example: A unit with Ld 6+ succeeds on a 2D6 result of 6 or higher.

entries.name: Battle-Shock Roll
entries.definition: A leadership roll to determine whether a unit becomes battle-shocked. During your Command phase, check units that are battle-shocked or at/below half strength.
entries.example: A squad reduced from 5 models to 2 models must test during the Command phase.

entries.name: Battle-Shocked
entries.definition: A unit that failed a battle-shock roll: its models’ OC becomes “–”, it cannot be targeted by its controller’s stratagems, and it cannot start or finish actions.
entries.example: A battle-shocked Scout Squad cannot count OC toward holding an objective.

entries.name: Half-Strength
entries.definition: At or below half starting model count, or for a one-model unit, its remaining wounds at or below half of its starting W; may trigger a Command phase battle-shock test.
entries.example: A 10-model squad reduced to 5 is at half strength.

entries.name: Destroyed
entries.definition: A model is destroyed when reduced to zero or fewer wounds, and a unit is destroyed when all its models are destroyed.
entries.example: A W3 Eradicator taking 3 damage from one attack is destroyed.

entries.name: Save vs Invulnerable Save
entries.definition: An armour save is modified by AP. An invulnerable save uses the listed InSv threshold instead, without AP.
entries.example: Against AP -3, a 4+ invulnerable save may be more reliable than 3+ armour.

entries.name: FNP vs Invulnerable Save
entries.definition: An invulnerable save attempts to stop the attack from causing damage; Feel No Pain is rolled for individual wounds that would be lost.
entries.example: Against D3 damage: roll one invulnerable save; if it fails, roll a Feel No Pain for each lost wound.

entries.name: Starting Strength
entries.definition: The number of models a unit had at the start of the first battle round; for one-model units, half-strength calculations instead use wounds.
entries.example: A unit starting with 6 models has starting strength 6.

entries.name: Benefit of Cover
entries.definition: In 11th edition, cover worsens the Ballistic Skill (BS) characteristic of a ranged attack against the target by 1, rather than directly adding to its saving throw.
entries.example: A BS 3+ ranged attacker effectively becomes BS 4+ against a unit with cover.

entries.name: Terrain Area
entries.definition: The defined footprint of a terrain piece or collection of pieces; influences movement, cover and often objectives.
entries.example: A ruin can sit inside a marked rectangular terrain footprint.

entries.name: Exposed Terrain
entries.definition: Terrain category that does not meaningfully obstruct models; examples include craters and scattered debris.
entries.example: A crater marked Exposed can be moved through normally.

entries.name: Light Terrain
entries.definition: Terrain category such as barricades or low walls; interacts with cover and obscuring without Dense movement restrictions.
entries.example: A barricade can block partial visibility.

entries.name: Dense Terrain
entries.definition: Terrain category for buildings, ruins, large containers and woods. It has more restrictive visibility and movement interactions.
entries.example: Infantry can move horizontally through a dense ruin; a tank has limitations.

entries.name: Line of Sight
entries.definition: An imaginary straight line 1 mm wide from any part of an observing model to any part of another, subject to terrain and special rules.
entries.example: A blocked line through a solid ground-floor window cannot establish sight.

entries.name: Hidden
entries.definition: Infantry/Beasts/Swarm models within a terrain area containing Dense terrain can become Hidden if their unit did not shoot this or previous turn. Hidden models are visible only within detection range.
entries.example: A Scout Squad sheltering quietly in a ruin may be invisible beyond the usual 15-inch detection range.

entries.name: Detection Range
entries.definition: How near an enemy must be to see a Hidden model. Normally 15 inches, with possible modifiers and special rules.
entries.example: A Hidden infantry model is not visible to an enemy 18 inches away under the standard detection range.

entries.name: Obscuring
entries.definition: Light/Dense terrain areas are Obscuring. If every line of sight between models crosses an intervening Obscuring area that neither is inside, the models cannot see each other.
entries.example: A ruin between your Lancer and its target can block the shot even if the terrain piece has an opening.

entries.name: Solid
entries.definition: Dense terrain blocks sight through enclosed gaps 3 inches or less above ground level, such as windows and doors.
entries.example: A ground-floor ruin window cannot be used as a firing slit.

entries.name: Gone to Ground
entries.definition: Wahapedia Appendix condition: a qualifying Hidden model not fully visible due to intervening Dense terrain can reduce its detection range by 3 inches.
entries.example: A normally 15-inch detection range may shrink to 12 inches.

entries.name: Plunging Fire
entries.definition: Ranged attacks against a visible target with at least one model on ground level improve BS by 1 when fired from a terrain surface at least 3 inches high, or by Towering within 12 inches.
entries.example: A marine shooting down from a 3-inch-high ruin improves BS from 3+ to 2+.

entries.name: Terrain and Movement
entries.definition: Infantry/Beasts/Swarm can traverse Dense terrain; Mobile adds horizontal movement benefits; other models face height and floor limitations.
entries.example: Deathwing infantry can move through solid ruin walls under the Dense movement rules.

entries.name: Objective
entries.definition: A location described by a mission that players contest; most 11th core missions use a terrain area as the objective.
entries.example: Hold the objective in a ruin with more OC than the opponent.

entries.name: Terrain Objective
entries.definition: The terrain area associated with an objective location in the mission’s deployment map; models within the area are in range of the objective.
entries.example: Your Scout Squad inside an objective’s designated terrain area can contest it.

entries.name: Objective Marker
entries.definition: If an objective lacks a terrain area, represent it with a flat 40 mm marker. Its control range is specified in the Appendix.
entries.example: The marker is 40 mm wide; normally count models within 3 inches horizontally/5 vertically of it.

entries.name: Level of Control
entries.definition: Add the OC characteristic of all eligible models in your army within range of the objective; compare totals with your opponent’s.
entries.example: Your OC5 beats enemy OC3, so you control it.

entries.name: Control an Objective
entries.definition: At end of phase/turn, the side with greater level of control holds the objective; equal levels normally mean neither player controls it.
entries.example: A side with 6 OC beats a side with 5 OC.

entries.name: Secured Objective
entries.definition: Certain rules make an objective remain controlled even after your units leave, until the opponent exceeds your control level at end of a phase.
entries.example: A squad secures an objective, then moves off it while control persists.

entries.name: Mission
entries.definition: The mission defines deployment, objectives, victory conditions and other rules; it is separate from the core rules book.
entries.example: Use a mission deck for the scenario and scoring rules.

entries.name: Victory Points (VP)
entries.definition: Points awarded by a mission for completing objectives or scoring tasks; their exact amounts are mission-specific.
entries.example: Score primary or secondary points as instructed by your selected mission cards.

entries.name: Primary Mission
entries.definition: Mission-specific main victory condition, usually tied to controlling or completing key objectives.
entries.example: Score points as stated by the chosen primary mission card.

entries.name: Secondary Mission
entries.definition: Mission-specific additional scoring task; actual timing and conditions come from the mission pack.
entries.example: A card might reward completing a tactical objective rather than simply holding territory.

entries.name: Deployment Zone
entries.definition: The area assigned by the mission for initial placement; many movement, infiltrator and reserve rules refer to it.
entries.example: Set up ordinary units in your assigned zone unless another ability allows otherwise.

entries.name: Battle Round
entries.definition: One round in which each player takes a full turn, preceded and followed by round-start and round-end steps.
entries.example: A five-round game normally gives each player five turns.

entries.name: Player Turn
entries.definition: A player’s Start of Turn step, five phases (Command, Movement, Shooting, Charge, Fight), and End of Turn step.
entries.example: After your Fight phase, your opponent takes their turn.

entries.name: Start / End of Turn
entries.definition: Timing points for resolving abilities; end-of-turn effects are resolved before mission end-of-turn scoring as described in rules.
entries.example: Check whether an ability says end of phase, end of turn or end of battle round.

entries.name: Command Phase
entries.definition: First phase of a player turn: both players gain 1 Core CP, the active player makes required battle-shock rolls, then command abilities resolve.
entries.example: Both sides get 1 CP at the start of the active player’s Command phase.

entries.name: Command Point (CP)
entries.definition: A resource spent on stratagems. Both players gain 1 Core CP during each player’s Command phase.
entries.example: Spend 1 CP on Command Re-roll when its trigger occurs.

entries.name: Core CP
entries.definition: The one Command Point granted to each player in the Gain Core CP step; it behaves like ordinary CP.
entries.example: You gain one CP in your turn’s Command phase and another in your opponent’s.

entries.name: Stratagem
entries.definition: A tactical rule with CP cost, WHEN, TARGET, EFFECT and restrictions. Generally the same stratagem cannot be used twice in the same phase, and a unit can be targeted by only one stratagem per phase.
entries.example: You use Fire Overwatch on your opponent’s Movement phase.

entries.name: Command Re-roll
entries.definition: Core 1CP stratagem: re-roll a permitted advance, charge, damage, hazard, hit, save, wound or attack-count roll. For a charge, re-roll the full 2D6.
entries.example: Reroll a failed charge roll for your Knights.

entries.name: Epic Challenge
entries.definition: Core 1CP stratagem: when your Character unit is selected to fight, give one Character model’s melee weapons Precision for that phase.
entries.example: Let an attached Character try to target an enemy leader during melee.

entries.name: Insane Bravery
entries.definition: Core 1CP stratagem: automatically succeed a battle-shock roll just before rolling in your Command phase; once per battle.
entries.example: Keep a depleted objective holder from becoming battle-shocked.

entries.name: Explosives (stratagem)
entries.definition: Core 1CP: in your Shooting phase, an eligible Explosives/Grenades unit picks a visible unengaged enemy within 8 inches and rolls six dice; each 4+ inflicts a mortal wound.
entries.example: Your eligible Scouts throw explosives at a nearby enemy unit.

entries.name: Crushing Impact
entries.definition: Core 1CP after a Monster/Vehicle charges. Roll a number of dice equal to one engaged model’s T; each 1 wounds your own unit, each 5+ inflicts a mortal wound on the enemy (max six).
entries.example: A Dreadnought can deal impact mortals when charging, risking self-damage.

entries.name: Rapid Ingress (stratagem)
entries.definition: Core 1CP: at the end of the opponent’s Movement phase, bring in one eligible reserve unit with an ingress move; not in battle round one.
entries.example: Appear with an eligible Deep Strike unit on the opponent’s turn.

entries.name: Fire Overwatch
entries.definition: Core 1CP: at the end of the opponent’s Movement phase, an unengaged non-Titanic unit shoots using the restricted Snap Shooting type.
entries.example: Your Hellblasters fire at one eligible enemy within 24 inches, hitting on natural 6s.

entries.name: Smokescreen
entries.definition: Core 1CP at the start of enemy Shooting: a friendly Smoke unit grants cover to itself and units screened by its models until end of phase.
entries.example: A Smoke vehicle makes incoming shooting less accurate.

entries.name: Heroic Intervention
entries.definition: Core 1CP at the end of the enemy Charge phase: an eligible friendly unit resolves a charge with either Leap to Defend or an extra-cost Into the Fray mode.
entries.example: Your Knights may counter-charge after the enemy’s Charge phase, subject to eligibility.

entries.name: Counteroffensive
entries.definition: Core 2CP: in your opponent’s Fight phase just after an enemy fights, give one eligible friendly unit Fights First and select it to fight next.
entries.example: Interrupt the enemy’s planned order of melee activation.

entries.name: Action
entries.definition: A special task defined by a rule or mission, with STARTS, UNITS, USE LIMIT, COMPLETES and EFFECT. Starting one normally stops shooting or charging that turn.
entries.example: A unit completes a mission-specified action to earn points.

entries.name: Eligible to Start an Action
entries.definition: Usually cannot be off-table, Aircraft/Fortification, battle-shocked, OC0/–, engaged (unless Titanic), already acting, or have Advanced/Fallen Back that turn.
entries.example: A battle-shocked Scout Squad cannot start a mission action.

entries.name: Completing an Action
entries.definition: An action finishes at its listed time if the unit does not make a disqualifying move or leave the battlefield; then apply its Effect.
entries.example: An action that completes end of turn is interrupted by a normal move.

entries.name: Stratagem Timing
entries.definition: The WHEN instruction specifies an exact point, phase or trigger for spending CP; check this before using the stratagem.
entries.example: Fire Overwatch is at the end of the opponent’s Movement phase, not when they begin moving.

entries.name: Strategic Reserves
entries.definition: Units held off-table to arrive later. Up to 50% of the battle’s points limit may normally start in Strategic Reserves.
entries.example: Hold a unit to bring in from a battlefield edge on a later turn.

entries.name: Ingress Move
entries.definition: Set up a reserve unit wholly within 6 inches of a battlefield edge and more than 8 inches horizontally from enemies. Before round three, not in enemy deployment zone.
entries.example: Deep Strike can override where the unit arrives but still uses the ingress-move framework.

entries.name: Reserves Timing
entries.definition: Strategic reserves normally cannot arrive until battle round two; those not arrived by the end of round three are normally destroyed (with stated exceptions).
entries.example: Bring reserve Eradicators onto the board on round two or three when eligible.

entries.name: Repositioned Unit
entries.definition: A unit moved from the board back into Strategic Reserves by a rule; existing ongoing effects and applicable movement history may persist.
entries.example: An ability removes a squad and returns it in a later phase.

entries.name: Embark
entries.definition: After eligible normal, Advance or Fall Back movement, all models within 3 inches of a transport may embark if the transport allows them and has capacity.
entries.example: Move an eligible squad next to a transport, then remove it from the board as embarked.

entries.name: Transport Capacity
entries.definition: The maximum permitted passengers and types described on a transport’s datasheet.
entries.example: A transport cannot take more models than its capacity allows.

entries.name: Disembark
entries.definition: An embarked unit sets up outside its transport in the Movement phase using Rapid, Tactical or Combat Disembark, according to circumstances.
entries.example: Passengers exit their transport then follow their applicable disembark mode.

entries.name: Rapid Disembark
entries.definition: When transport Normal-moved or Ingressed this phase: passengers set up within 3 inches; normally cannot charge that turn.
entries.example: Passengers leave a transport after it moved.

entries.name: Tactical Disembark
entries.definition: Passengers exit a stationary/not-yet-moved transport within 3 inches and then make a normal or Advance move.
entries.example: Exit first, then move the infantry squad.

entries.name: Combat Disembark
entries.definition: When required, passengers roll hazards and may set up within 6 inches, even engaged with enemies engaged with the transport; they become battle-shocked and cannot charge.
entries.example: Troops spill out into a contested combat.

entries.name: Emergency Disembark
entries.definition: When transport is destroyed, its passengers roll hazards, set up as close as possible within 6 inches, become battle-shocked and cannot charge that turn.
entries.example: A destroyed transport forces the occupants out and may kill models that cannot fit.

entries.name: Attached Unit
entries.definition: A Leader and/or Support unit joined to a Bodyguard unit; acts as one unit and normally uses bodyguards’ Toughness while they remain.
entries.example: Azrael joins an eligible squad, and the combination acts as one unit.

entries.name: Bodyguard Unit
entries.definition: The unit that a Leader or Support may join; its models generally shield attached Characters during damage allocation.
entries.example: Inner Circle Companions can act as bodyguards if their leader attachment rules permit.

entries.name: Aura Ability
entries.definition: An ability affecting models or units within a given distance. The source is within its own aura; identical aura instances do not stack on one unit.
entries.example: A Character grants a nearby friendly squad an aura bonus.

entries.name: Faction Ability
entries.definition: An army rule common to qualifying faction units; normally functions when the selected army faction matches the unit’s faction keyword.
entries.example: Combat Doctrines for eligible Adeptus Astartes units.

entries.name: Wargear Ability
entries.definition: An ability granted by an item a model or unit carries; if tied to a bearer model, it stops when the bearer is destroyed.
entries.example: A squad’s special banner gives a buff while its bearer remains alive.

entries.name: Psychic Ability
entries.definition: An ability tagged Psychic; wounds it inflicts are treated as coming from a psychic attack.
entries.example: A psychic ability that directly causes lost wounds counts as psychic damage for interactions.

entries.name: Flying / FLY
entries.definition: A Flying unit may “take to the skies” when making certain moves. It loses 2 inches of max distance but can pass through all units/terrain and ignore vertical distance.
entries.example: A FLY unit with a maximum 12-inch move taking to the skies moves up to 10 inches.

entries.name: Taking to the Skies
entries.definition: Optional flight mode declared before certain moves; subtract 2 inches movement, ignore vertical movement and fly through models and terrain. Hover cancels the penalty.
entries.example: A flying vehicle can pass over a ruin without counting its height.

entries.name: Surge Move
entries.definition: A special triggered move towards the closest enemy. Usually requires unengaged, not battle-shocked and not already moved this phase; cannot move again that phase.
entries.example: A faction ability lets a squad surge D6 inches toward the closest foe.

entries.name: Aircraft
entries.definition: Special units that start in reserves, move primarily via Ingress and leave the board into reserves at the end of the opponent’s turn; can only fight Flying units.
entries.example: Aircraft obey separate placement and engagement rules from ordinary tanks.

entries.name: Frame
entries.definition: For models with FRAME, measure distances to/from the closest point on the model, rather than necessarily the base.
entries.example: A vehicle without a base uses its hull for measurements.

entries.name: Monster / Vehicle Movement
entries.definition: When making a Normal or Advance move, Monster/Vehicle models may move through other models except other Monsters/Vehicles, subject to other rules.
entries.example: A Dreadnought can move through infantry models in some circumstances.

entries.name: INFANTRY
entries.definition: A model/unit keyword. Has specific benefits when moving through Dense terrain, hiding and interacting with other rules.
entries.example: Hellblasters are Infantry.

entries.name: VEHICLE
entries.definition: Unit keyword for vehicles; triggers some movement, shooting and Anti-Vehicle interactions.
entries.example: A Gladiator Lancer has the Vehicle keyword.

entries.name: MONSTER
entries.definition: Unit keyword for very large creatures; shares several battlefield rules with Vehicles.
entries.example: An enemy Magnus model may use Monster-related rules based on its datasheet.

entries.name: CHARACTER
entries.definition: Keyword for named leaders and officers. Affects Attached Units, allocation and some stratagems.
entries.example: Azrael and Lion El’Jonson are Characters.

entries.name: BATTLELINE
entries.definition: Unit tag used by army building and missions; its rules depend on the applicable roster or mission.
entries.example: A Battleline unit may be treated differently for list construction.

entries.name: BEASTS
entries.definition: Keyword for beast models; shares some terrain movement and hiding rules with Infantry/Swarm.
entries.example: Beasts can traverse Dense terrain vertically under applicable rules.

entries.name: SWARM
entries.definition: Keyword for swarming models; shares some terrain rules with Infantry/Beasts.
entries.example: Swarm models in a Dense terrain area may qualify as Hidden.

entries.name: FLY
entries.definition: Keyword marking a model/unit as Flying; enables Taking to the Skies and affects Aircraft melee eligibility.
entries.example: A qualifying flying model can ignore terrain height when taking to the skies.

entries.name: MOBILE
entries.definition: Keyword affecting movement through Dense terrain features: Mobile can move horizontally through Dense terrain.
entries.example: A Super-Heavy Walker may temporarily gain Mobile.

entries.name: TITANIC
entries.definition: Keyword for especially large units, referenced by special restrictions and exceptions.
entries.example: Titans cannot be chosen for the core Fire Overwatch stratagem.

entries.name: TOWERING
entries.definition: Keyword providing a Plunging Fire condition when shooting ground-level targets within 12 inches.
entries.example: A Towering model may improve BS against a close ground-level target.

entries.name: TRANSPORT
entries.definition: Keyword for a unit capable of carrying other units, subject to its capacity and permitted passengers.
entries.example: An Impulsor may carry eligible troops.

entries.name: DEDICATED TRANSPORT
entries.definition: A transport subtype; Scouts rules have a special interaction when everyone embarked has Scouts.
entries.example: A qualifying Dedicated Transport may make a pre-battle Scout move.

entries.name: AIRCRAFT (keyword)
entries.definition: Keyword identifying models using the specialised Aircraft rules.
entries.example: Aircraft deploy into reserves rather than on-table.

entries.name: WALKER
entries.definition: Keyword distinguishing walker-type Vehicles for certain rules such as Heroic Intervention targeting.
entries.example: A walker Vehicle can qualify for rules that exclude other Vehicles.

entries.name: SMOKE
entries.definition: Keyword allowing a unit to be targeted by the Smokescreen core stratagem.
entries.example: A Smoke vehicle uses Smokescreen when the opponent starts Shooting.

entries.name: EXPLOSIVES
entries.definition: A keyword permitting the use of the Explosives core stratagem if other conditions are met.
entries.example: Eradicators have Explosives in their current Wahapedia datasheet.

entries.name: GRENADES
entries.definition: A keyword that can also qualify a unit for the Explosives core stratagem.
entries.example: A Grenades unit may use the 1CP Explosives stratagem.

entries.name: PSYKER
entries.definition: Unit keyword for psychic models and interactions, including Anti-Psyker weapons.
entries.example: [ANTI-PSYKER 2+] makes wound rolls of 2+ critical against a Psyker unit.

entries.name: FORTIFICATION
entries.definition: Keyword for fortifications; normally cannot perform actions or be placed in strategic reserves as ordinary units.
entries.example: A static fortification is excluded from ordinary strategic reserve placement.

entries.name: ADEPTUS ASTARTES
entries.definition: The Space Marines faction keyword used to determine many army and detachment rules.
entries.example: Your Dark Angels units share Adeptus Astartes faction eligibility.

entries.name: DARK ANGELS
entries.definition: Chapter keyword identifying your Space Marine faction, used for army restrictions and detachment/unit rules.
entries.example: Lion El’Jonson and Azrael belong to Dark Angels.

entries.name: DEATHWING / RAVENWING
entries.definition: Dark Angels subgroup keywords on applicable datasheets; interactions depend on the relevant faction/detachment abilities, not on a universal core effect.
entries.example: Deathwing Knights and Ravenwing Black Knights use different subgroup keywords.

entries.name: EPIC HERO
entries.definition: Keyword or roster classification with unit-selection implications; check the current 11th-edition muster-armies and faction material for restrictions.
entries.example: Named legendary Characters such as Lion El’Jonson are typically Epic Heroes.

entries.name: GRAVIS
entries.definition: Space Marine armour keyword used by some detachments and special unit abilities.
entries.example: Eradicator Squad models have the Gravis keyword.

entries.name: PHOBOS
entries.definition: Space Marine armour/scout keyword used by some abilities and detachments.
entries.example: Some reconnaissance squads have Phobos.

entries.name: Hunter Weapon Profile
entries.definition: Some weapons have a specially labeled Hunter profile that can target only the listed unit keywords. Choose the profile before selecting targets. This is not [ANTI-X Y+].
entries.example: Your Eradicators’ Melta Rifle - Hunter can target Monster/Vehicle and has a different BS/S profile.

entries.name: Multiple Weapon Profiles
entries.definition: If a weapon has alternative profiles, select one eligible profile before attacks; that choice determines the attacks it makes.
entries.example: Choose Melta Rifle - Hunter only against the keyword(s) specified.

entries.name: Mixed Keywords
entries.definition: A unit has the union of all keywords on its constituent models, but a model does not gain the other models’ keywords.
entries.example: An attached Psyker Character makes the whole unit a Psyker unit for targeting with Anti-Psyker.

entries.name: Persisting Effects
entries.definition: Timed effects can remain on a unit that embarks or enters reserves; track their duration if it returns to the battlefield.
entries.example: A buff lasting until next turn remains if the unit temporarily leaves the board.

entries.name: Not on the Battlefield
entries.definition: Embarked, reserve and otherwise off-table units generally cannot act as if on the battlefield unless a rule explicitly says so.
entries.example: An embarked squad normally cannot target enemies with its own guns unless a rule permits.

entries.name: Revived Models
entries.definition: Rules that revive/add models must follow the Appendix’s placement, unit-composition and wound-restoration restrictions.
entries.example: Returning a slain model does not necessarily refresh a used One Shot weapon.

entries.name: Characteristic Modifiers
entries.definition: When changing stats, modifiers apply in a defined order with minimum/maximum limits. Improving BS or Sv lowers its X+ number, while improving AP makes it more negative.
entries.example: Improve 3+ BS by 1 → 2+; improve AP -1 by 1 → AP -2.

entries.name: Weapon Abilities Do Not Stack
entries.definition: Two instances of the same bracketed ability do not add together, even with different X or target keywords; choose one.
entries.example: [ANTI-VEHICLE 4+] and [ANTI-INFANTRY 2+] on one weapon cannot both operate simultaneously as duplicate Anti abilities.

entries.name: Criticals vs Automatic Hits
entries.definition: Automatically generated hits or wounds are not critical hits/wounds unless a rule says they are, so they do not automatically re-trigger other critical abilities.
entries.example: Extra hits from Sustained Hits are hits, not fresh critical hits.

entries.name: Overwatch and Critical Hits
entries.definition: Wahapedia’s 11th-edition Snap Shooting clarification says the required unmodified-6 hits are not critical hits; critical-triggered effects cannot be assumed to activate.
entries.example: Sustained Hits on an Overwatch gun does not trigger from its ordinary Snap Shooting sixes.

entries.name: Action and Shooting
entries.definition: Action eligibility is not the same as having a gun. A model with no ranged weapon may still be eligible to shoot for the purpose of other rules.
entries.example: A gunless unit can be eligible for a mission action if all other restrictions are met.

entries.name: Ability Aura Overlap
entries.definition: Two copies of the same Aura ability affecting one unit do not stack; separate, differently named Auras may apply together.
entries.example: Two identical buffing Characters do not double one named Aura effect.

entries.name: End-of-Phase Objective Check
entries.definition: Objective control is determined at the end of each phase and turn before resolving other “end of phase/turn” rules.
entries.example: Determine who controls a point before scoring triggered at end of the phase.

entries.name: Bearer
entries.definition: The individual model equipped with a weapon, enhancement or wargear item.
entries.example: A particular marine may be the bearer of a special weapon.

entries.name: Damaged X
entries.definition: An additional 11th-edition ability on updated Wahapedia, in the form Damaged X: when the model has X or fewer wounds remaining, its attacks suffer -1 to hit.
entries.example: A vehicle with Damaged 4 has -1 to hit while at 4 or fewer remaining wounds.
entries.note: Added to Wahapedia online core rules after the uploaded PDF’s chapter 24 ended at 24.38.

entries.name: Conditional Keyword Lists
entries.definition: Slashes (INFANTRY/BEASTS) or an “or” list mean any one keyword; adjacent separate keywords may require every listed keyword.
entries.example: INFANTRY/MONSTER means either; ADEPTUS ASTARTES INFANTRY means both.

entries.name: Current vs Starting Wounds
entries.definition: A lone model tests half-strength against remaining wounds relative to its W characteristic; multi-model units use remaining model count.
entries.example: A single vehicle with W10 at W5 is at half strength.

entries.name: Eradicator Hunter Profile
entries.definition: Your Eradicators’ Melta Rifles can select a Hunter: Monster/Vehicle profile with better BS and Strength but restricted to those targets. Check the current unit profile for exact stats.
entries.example: Wahapedia: normal Melta Rifle BS3+ S10; Hunter Melta Rifle BS2+ S12 against Monsters/Vehicles.

entries.name: Hellblasters and Hazardous
entries.definition: Hellblaster plasma is a good reason to know Hazardous and hazard rolls; use the exact current plasma incinerator profile to see when the keyword applies.
entries.example: After resolving a unit’s Hazardous weapon attacks, roll one hazard die for each selected Hazardous weapon.

entries.name: Deathwing Knights and Charges
entries.definition: Deathwing Knights are melee specialists: plan the 2D6 charge, legal engagement, Fights First after charging, and pile-in/fight/consolidation sequence.
entries.example: Move/charge → pile-in up to 3 inches → fight → consolidate up to 3 inches when eligible.

entries.name: Scouts and Objectives
entries.definition: Your Scout Squad can help you screen early space, contest objectives and start eligible mission actions. Distinguish its Scouts ability from the generic INFANTRY keyword.
entries.example: Use pre-battle Scout movement if the unit’s current datasheet grants Scouts.

entries.name: Wrath of the Rock
entries.definition: Your selected Dark Angels detachment has its own detachment rule, enhancements and stratagems beyond this core dictionary. Confirm details on the 11th-edition faction page.
entries.example: Wahapedia lists Dutiful Tenacity and Wrath of the Rock stratagems.

entries.name: Assault Brethren
entries.definition: Your selected detachment adds a separate set of detachment benefits. The name is not the same as the [ASSAULT] weapon ability.
entries.example: Wahapedia lists Assault Mastery for this detachment.

entries.name: Combat Doctrines
entries.definition: A Space Marine faction rule: select a doctrine at the start of your Command phase; its rule applies to eligible models for the stated duration. The details depend on current faction rules.
entries.example: Devastator Doctrine can grant [ASSAULT] to ranged attacks of eligible units.

entries.name: Lion El’Jonson
entries.definition: Your Warlord is a named Dark Angels Character. His exact datasheet abilities, keywords and melee weapons are faction-specific.
entries.example: For his attacks, look up his current Fealty/Arma Luminis profiles alongside core keywords.
